sections.title: The Basics
sections.body: An IPv4 address is a 32-bit number written as four blocks (octets) from 0 to 255, separated by dots. Every device that wants to use IP needs one. Example: 192.168.1.50.

sections.title: Two Parts: Network + Host
sections.body: Every IP splits into two parts. The NETWORK part says which street you live on; the HOST part says which house on that street. The subnet mask decides where the split happens.

sections.title: How Many Hosts Fit?
sections.body: Count host bits and use 2^bits minus 2. Why minus 2? One address is reserved as the network name and one as broadcast.
sections.code:
/24 -> 8 host bits -> 2^8 - 2 = 254 usable hosts
/30 -> 2 host bits -> 2^2 - 2 = 2 usable hosts

sections.title: Rules to Remember
points: Each octet ranges from 0 to 255 only.
Hosts on the SAME network need DIFFERENT IPs.
Two devices can share an IP only on DIFFERENT networks.
sections.tip: 💡 Exam tip: practice ONE binary-to-decimal conversion and the whole topic unlocks.
